description:
Threat Incursion

v0.4.0 - the swarm colonizes the sector - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

Download

ThreatIncursion-0.4.0.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher.

Pogo's explanation

The Threat can be configured to spawn at game start at a fringe world, but this is a super hardcore start. The default is that they spawn once you finish abyssal questline or a colony you control reaches size 6.

The Threat are slow to spread but obviously snowball as they can spread from each system they colonise after a period of seeding then early development. To combat this their colonies are easy to kill in the early stages but much harder as they increase in size.

Honestly there's a lot to this mod and you will need to be tactical with how you fight them. Colonies can be starved of resources by cutting off their supply chains. In general the Threat need a lot of rare ores so targeting their mining and refining is a good strategy. Their ground defences are extremely strong, lore reason provided being most of the their structures and populace hide underground. You *can* sat bomb them but the impact is low and the fuel cost extreme. Tac bombing is more effective but doesnt completely take their ground defences offline like it normally would. The most effective way to directly kill a colony is to raid it with marines and target the fabrication core. While this is down they cannot produce defence swarms and the colony will slow decline and drop through colony sizes (2-8) until it reaches size 1 and decolonises. If the disruption of the core ends this effect will reverse and they will start growing again and defensive sweets will resume production.

The cost of a wiping out a single colony is very high. But targeted strikes on their fuel and mining will weaken the whole empire. They have a completely closed economy and are dependent on their own network for imports. If a colony cant produce metals and fuel it will import via the usual accessibility markers, so you can also disrupt the megaport to reduce a single colonies ability to produce fleets.

The core worlds will fight back and send purge expeditions. These will attack the defensive swarms and perform tac bombs and raids if they have the fuel and marine reserves to do so. You can also commission your own purge expeditions at great cost assuming you have the military capability and your closest military colony is within range of an infected system.

The locations of the threat wont be revealed to you until you discover the system, or the threat sends out a raid. The threat raid using their defensive swarms, so a colony that has just sent out a raiding party is susceptible to attack. There are bounties that are issued by the core worlds for immediate objectives (destroying colony within strike range of the core worlds) as well as strategic (disrupt critical mining/fuel production).

Claude's explanation

The Threat founds real, growing colonies on the fringe that mine, refine, forge and grow, running a closed hive economy that builds every fleet they field.That economy is fully interdictable - cut their rare ore, fuel, metals or machinery and ship quality, strike range, garrisons and growth all suffer across the whole network.Hive worlds run three industry "organs": the Fabrication Core (growth and heavy machinery), the Swarm Nexus (grows Defense Swarms and musters expeditions), and marine-free ground defenses and batteries fed on metals and machinery.Expeditions are mustered from a colony's own Defense Swarms - kill its swarms and you have grounded it. Each expedition sweeps its whole target system, bombarding every world at most once.An expedition can be stopped before launch by raiding or bombing its staging colony while the fleet is still being fabricated.Worlds the swarm destroys, it colonizes.Colonies die only through Hive Vitality decline (fabrication x supply). Below 35% vitality the colony declines toward size 1; bombardment cannot reduce population directly.Siege loop: defeat the Defense Swarms, tac-bomb to suppress the ground defenses, disrupt the Fabrication Core (marines or a saturation pass), then hold the pressure. Decline accrues continuously and accelerates; small colonies die fast, capitals resist.Economic alternative: strangle a hub colony's supply chain and several sister colonies slide into decline at once.The sector fights back - faction task forces hit staging garrisons, NPC siege expeditions bombard and raid hives, and two-tier live bounty boards open from phase 3.Commission your own siege expeditions from the infested-system intel: sized to the target, built with your doctrine and blueprints, priced by flotilla size and distance.Every siege, decline and economy number is configurable via LunaLib (Shift+F2) or data/config/settings.json.For Starsector 0.98a-RC8. LunaLib optional. Vanilla-only, no hard dependencies. Safe to add to an existing save; removing it mid-incursion breaks the save.

Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experience

Standalone, safe to add mid-save, can be run together or separately.

Threat Incursion — the threat colonizes the sector and invades the core worlds. Disrupt their supply chains and besiege the entrenched hives into decline.
Commerce Wars — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
Piracy Reworked — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.
Remnant Retribution — a late-game colony crisis.
Useful Planetary Shield — planetary shields finally do something: they absorb orbital bombardment.

Disclaimer: This post and these mods were written using Claude's Fable AI model. Design and testing by pogoman.

v0.4.0 - the swarm colonizes the sector - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

Download

ThreatIncursion-0.4.0.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher.

There are bounties that are issued by the core worlds for immediate objectives (destroying colony within strike range of the core worlds) as well as strategic (disrupt critical mining/fuel production).


Claude's explanation

  • The Threat founds real, growing colonies on the fringe that mine, refine, forge and grow, running a closed hive economy that builds every fleet they field.
  • That economy is fully interdictable - cut their rare ore, fuel, metals or machinery and ship quality, strike range, garrisons and growth all suffer across the whole network.
  • Hive worlds run three industry "organs": the Fabrication Core (growth and heavy machinery), the Swarm Nexus (grows Defense Swarms and musters expeditions), and marine-free ground defenses and batteries fed on metals and machinery.
  • Expeditions are mustered from a colony's own Defense Swarms - kill its swarms and you have grounded it. Each expedition sweeps its whole target system, bombarding every world at most once.
  • An expedition can be stopped before launch by raiding or bombing its staging colony while the fleet is still being fabricated.
  • Worlds the swarm destroys, it colonizes.
  • Colonies die only through Hive Vitality decline (fabrication x supply). Below 35% vitality the colony declines toward size 1; bombardment cannot reduce population directly.
  • Siege loop: defeat the Defense Swarms, tac-bomb to suppress the ground defenses, disrupt the Fabrication Core (marines or a saturation pass), then hold the pressure. Decline accrues continuously and accelerates; small colonies die fast, capitals resist.
  • Economic alternative: strangle a hub colony's supply chain and several sister colonies slide into decline at once.
  • The sector fights back - faction task forces hit staging garrisons, NPC siege expeditions bombard and raid hives, and two-tier live bounty boards open from phase 3.
  • Commission your own siege expeditions from the infested-system intel: sized to the target, built with your doctrine and blueprints, priced by flotilla size and distance.
  • Every siege, decline and economy number is configurable via LunaLib (Shift+F2) or data/config/settings.json.
  • For Starsector 0.98a-RC8. LunaLib optional. Vanilla-only, no hard dependencies. Safe to add to an existing save; removing it mid-incursion breaks the save.

  • Piracy Reworked — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.
  • Remnant Retribution — a late-game colony crisis.

aiDescription: Introduces a swarm faction that establishes growing colonies on fringe worlds, running a closed economy dependent on rare ores and internal supply chains. Players must disrupt these supply lines or conduct high-cost raids targeting fabrication cores to reduce colony vitality and force decolonization. The system includes dynamic expeditions, bounties, and configurable settings via LunaLib.
